Accumulated local effects of fitted learners in held-out folds

Source: R/csdg_effect.R
csdg_effect.Rd

Computes, for each learner and fold of a csdg_fit() result, the accumulated local effect (ALE) of numeric predictors in the held-out fold and its change between two percentiles of the predictor (default 10th and 90th). Look at the result with print() and plot() before stating a direction with claim_direction().

The ALE is computed on intervals quantile intervals of the predictor in the held-out fold: within each interval, the predictions at its upper and lower boundary are differenced and averaged over the rows in the interval, and the averages are accumulated. For classification, the predictions are probabilities of the positive class. The change is the difference of the accumulated effect between the two percentiles; the summary averages it over folds and reports the corrected resampled 95% interval (csdg_learner_pfi_interval()) descriptively.

Usage

csdg_effect(fits, features = NULL, probs = c(0.1, 0.9), intervals = 20L)

# S3 method for class 'CSDGEffect'
format(x, learner = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'CSDGEffect'
print(x, learner = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'CSDGEffect'
as.data.table(
  x,
  keep.rownames = FALSE,
  ...,
  level = c("summary", "change", "curve")
)

# S3 method for class 'CSDGEffect'
plot(x, learner = NULL, features = NULL, ...)

Arguments

fits

A csdg_fit() result.

features

For plot(): predictors shown; defaults to all.

probs

Two increasing probabilities strictly between 0 and 1: the percentiles between which the change is measured.

intervals

Number of quantile intervals of the ALE.

x

A CSDGEffect object.

learner

For print() and plot(): names or labels of the learners shown; defaults to all.

...

Ignored.

keep.rownames

Ignored.

level

For as.data.table(): "summary", "change" (per fold), or "curve" (ALE per fold).

Value

A CSDGEffect list with fits, features, probs, intervals, changes (one row per learner, predictor, and fold), curves (the ALE per fold), and summary (mean change, corrected interval, and the number of folds with a positive change per learner and predictor). as.data.table() returns one of the tables.

See also

claim_direction(), csdg_check()

Examples

set.seed(1)
n = 200
x = data.frame(a = rnorm(n), b = rnorm(n))
x$y = 2 * x$a + rnorm(n)
task = mlr3::as_task_regr(x, target = "y", id = "toy")
fits = csdg_fit(task, list(tree = mlr3::lrn("regr.rpart")), folds = 3, seed = 1)
eff = csdg_effect(fits)
eff
#> <CSDGEffect> ALE change of the prediction between the 10th and 90th percentiles in held-out folds; 3 folds
#> decision tree:
#>   predictor   mean change   corrected 95% interval   folds with a positive change
#>   a                  4.24            [0.719, 7.76]                            3/3
#>   b                     0                   [0, 0]                            0/3
#> The interval is reported descriptively; claim_direction() states a direction and csdg_check() checks it.
